title: On-demand pricing fallback and entitlement simulation PRD
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a PRD for an on-demand pricing fallback mechanism combined with an entitlement simulator that lets product, sales, and engineering safely rehearse entitlement changes (quota increases/decreases, grace credits, and overage policies) and validate downstream billing invoices before pushing changes to production. The goal is to lower risk when introducing new soft-cap behaviors and to provide an automated acceptance suite that verifies cost/charge correctness across rate-limit and quota permutations.

Background / problem:
- Engineering has shipped multiple quota/overage features (adaptive burst credits, per-route entitlements) but lacks a repeatable way to simulate their interactions end-to-end before enabling them account-by-account.
- Sales and support need visibility into how proposed entitlement changes affect invoice outcomes and product behavior (e.g., which requests get throttled, when fallback models are selected).
- Incidents have occurred when plan changes or emergency bursts were applied without a predictable billing outcome.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Implement a deterministic fallback pricing policy layer that is evaluated at request-time when primary entitlements are exhausted. The layer should support prioritized fallbacks (e.g., fall back to cheaper quantized model, fall back to pay-as-you-go tokens, fall back to throttling).
2) Build an entitlement simulator (web UI + API) that can run replayed traffic for a tenant against a proposed entitlement configuration and produce a simulated invoice and request-level outcome log.
3) Define billing acceptance criteria and integration tests that must pass before any new pricing/fallback policy is promoted to production.
4) Provide observability: per-simulation diffs, audit outputs, and a compare mode between current and candidate policy.

Non-goals:
- Changing core billing ledger storage format (out of scope for this ticket).
- Implementing new pricing tiers — this ticket provides tooling and flows; pricing numbers should be specified in separate PRDs.

Assumptions:
- We can reuse trace/replay data from the request logging pipeline (Kafka topic: request-events-v2) to drive simulations.
- The billing engine can run in a sandbox mode that produces invoices without committing to the ledger.
- Model fallback choices are expressible as ordered policies per-caller and per-route.

Requirements (functional):
A. Fallback policy engine:
  - Support policy definitions with ordered actions: [model-fallback, margin-surcharge, convert-to-payg, throttle].
  - Policies can be scoped at: global, plan, organization, caller-id, route, and model family.
  - Support rate limits with multiple windows (per-second, per-minute, per-hour) and quota buckets (monthly token budget, burst credits).
  - Expose an evaluation API: /v1/policy/evaluate that returns the chosen action and a deterministic explanation for a single request context.

B. Entitlement simulator:
  - Web UI for product/sales to upload a representative trace (or select an existing replay), choose a candidate entitlement config, and run a simulation.
  - API to submit simulation jobs and retrieve results. Jobs should support parallelization and streaming progress.
  - Output artifacts: simulated invoice (CSV/JSON), request-level outcome log (why each request used fallback/was throttled), charge breakdown by model/route, and diff to current config.
  - Simulation must run with synthetic enforcement of KV cache hits/misses to reflect prefix caching improvements.

C. Billing acceptance tests and gating:
  - New fallback policies must be accompanied by a simulation that demonstrates no customer will see >25% invoice delta relative to a baseline unless explicitly approved by Finance.
  - Integration tests: run a smoke simulation for a small account sample (internal test accounts) and verify ledger sandbox matches simulated invoice within 0.5% token rounding tolerance.
  - PRD must include a safety checklist: rollback plan, change window, notification to affected customers, and at least two SRE sign-offs.

D. Auditability and traceability:
  - All simulation runs must be logged with user, config snapshot, dataset used, and a permalink to results.
  - Policy evaluations in production must emit evaluation traces with policy-id and decision-reason fields.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
1) Fallback policy engine prototype implemented and documented: can be invoked with a single request context and returns decision + explanation. (Test: call /v1/policy/evaluate with 10 synthetic contexts)
2) Entitlement simulator UI + API implemented: can run a replay of 1M requests within a staging environment and produce a simulated invoice and per-request outcomes. (Test: run provided 'staging-replay-2026-02' trace)
3) Sandbox billing engine produces an invoice JSON that matches simulator output for test accounts within 0.5% tolerance. (Test: ledger-sandbox run compares to simulator CSV)
4) Automated acceptance test: for each candidate policy, an automated job runs simulation and fails promotion if >5% of test accounts exceed 10% invoice delta, or any account exceeds 25% delta without explicit Finance approval.
5) Documentation: a runbook describing how to use the simulator, common failure modes, and the rollback steps must be published to Confluence.
6) Observability: policy evaluation traces are visible in the Console tracing view and linked to the simulation output.

Instrumentation and metrics to add:
- Simulator: job_duration_seconds, replay_requests_processed, distinct_customers_simulated, simulation_invoice_total, simulation_invoice_delta_percent.
- Policy engine: policy_eval_count, policy_eval_latency_ms, policy_fallback_count (by action), policy_throttle_count.
- Acceptance gating: promotion_failure_count, reason labels (invoice_delta, test_failures, performance).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for policy engine decision tree and deterministic tie-breakers.
- Integration tests: run end-to-end using staging replay dataset.
- Load testing: verify simulator can complete 1M requests in < 2 hours on staging cluster; validate parallelization knobs.
- Manual review: Finance and Billing SME validate simulated invoices for a small set of enterprise customers.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag the policy engine evaluation API; deploy to staging only.
2) Ship simulator UI and API behind internal-only access for first 2 weeks.
3) Run a pilot with Billing and two Sales EBs using the simulator to rehearse three real customer plan changes.
4) After pilot sign-off and automated acceptance tests passing, enable simulation-driven gating for production policy promotions.

Edge cases and trade-offs:
- Trade-off: accuracy vs. runtime. Full-fidelity simulation (including KV cache dynamics) is slower but produces better invoice predictions. We'll expose fidelity tiers (fast approximate vs. slow full-fidelity).
- Edge case: sudden model pricing changes during replay windows — simulator will default to price-at-time-of-simulation unless 'use-historical-prices' is enabled.
- Edge case: cross-account credit pooling. Simulator will simulate both with and without pooling by default to surface differences.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Define approval thresholds for Finance (default limits above are proposals).
- Decide retention window for simulation artifacts (30 days vs. 180 days).
- Confirm which internal accounts are eligible for automated smoke promotion tests.
